moduleTitle: Automating mobile tests in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Explain how Testim Mobile extends Testim's AI-powered automation to native, hybrid, and cross-platform mobile apps.
Choose between Enhanced mode and Appium mode based on execution and compatibility needs.
Identify the native language support per platform (Android vs. iOS) for recording native apps.

elements.description: Testim Mobile supports native, hybrid and documented cross-platform frameworks. Use a mobile project separate from web, with a separate project for each mobile OS; language/framework coverage does not certify every application or interaction.

The Enhanced getting-started guide lists Android Java/Kotlin and iOS Objective-C/Swift. Recording uses the AUT Mirroring Viewer for one app on one device; prefer stable text targets. Validate replay rather than assuming that finding more elements automatically improves stability.

bulletPoints: Mobile projects are distinct from web and scoped to a single OS.
Native languages listed: Android Java/Kotlin, iOS Objective-C/Swift; validate the app/build/flow.

elements.description: Enhanced mode exposes richer hierarchy and a unified approach for supported app frameworks. It records and runs only on VMG virtual devices; vendor stability/speed claims are not guarantees for each flow.

Standard Appium compatibility mode supports appropriate local physical/virtual devices and Appium grids, including VMG. Verify the driver, build and required interactions: its documented hybrid/webview recording limitations do not mean Appium universally lacks hybrid support.

elements.title: Choosing a mode
items: VMG-only execution and compatible app/build → consider Enhanced mode; verify the required flow.
Local/physical/other-grid execution → use Standard Appium compatibility and configure its requirements.
Recording fixes the mode; changing execution mode requires re-recording, not a playback toggle.
VMG uses Android emulators and iOS simulators; provide compatible Android x86_64 and iOS simulator builds. Virtual runs do not validate real-device accessibility.

bulletPoints: Choose mode from execution/build/flow requirements rather than universal performance promises.
Enhanced requires VMG; Standard Appium supports configured local/other-grid execution.
Changing recorded mode requires re-recording. VMG virtual devices are not physical-device evidence.

examPitfalls.title: Recording in Enhanced mode, then expecting to run on a third-party Appium grid
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming a test recorded in Enhanced mode can be executed anywhere, including an external Appium-based grid.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Enhanced mode tests can be executed on VMG only. If execution on an external Appium-based grid or local devices is required, the test must be recorded in Appium mode instead.

examPitfalls.title: Trying to record a hybrid app's webview flow in Appium mode and being surprised by gaps
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Hitting recording limitations on a hybrid app/webview scenario while in Appium mode and assuming Testim itself can't handle it.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check the flow against the selected mode’s documented capabilities. Enhanced is an alternative for supported hybrid/webview flows on VMG, not a universal guarantee. Switching modes requires re-recording.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which native app languages does Testim Mobile support for recording on Android and iOS respectively?

options.text: Android: Java or Kotlin. iOS: Objective-C or Swift.
Android: Python only. iOS: Java only.
Native app languages are irrelevant to Testim Mobile.

practiceQuiz.hint: Each platform has two supported languages.
practiceQuiz.rationale: For Android devices, Testim supports Java or Kotlin native apps; for iOS devices, it supports Objective-C or Swift.

optionExplanations.A: These are the native languages listed in the Enhanced getting-started guide.
optionExplanations.B: The guide does not list Python/Java as that platform pair.
optionExplanations.D: The guide explicitly lists native language/framework requirements.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team needs their mobile tests to run on their own local devices and be compatible with an existing Appium-based grid. Which recording mode should they use?

options.text: Enhanced mode, since it's always the better choice.
Standard Appium compatibility mode, with the required driver/device/grid setup.
Neither mode supports local device execution.
It doesn't matter — both modes are executed identically.

practiceQuiz.hint: One mode is built specifically for Appium-grid and local-device compatibility.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Standard Appium compatibility permits these execution targets with suitable setup; Enhanced is limited to VMG virtual devices.

optionExplanations.A: Enhanced is limited to VMG rather than being universally best.
optionExplanations.B: Standard Appium supports the requested targets with appropriate setup.
optionExplanations.C: Standard Appium permits configured local execution.
optionExplanations.D: Modes differ in compatibility and recorded metadata.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the main execution trade-off of recording a mobile test in Enhanced mode?

options.text: It can only be executed on VMG, Testim's own mobile grid.
It cannot be executed at all, only recorded.
It requires a paid Appium license.
It only works for web apps, not mobile.

practiceQuiz.hint: It trades broad grid compatibility for stability/speed.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Enhanced-recorded tests run on VMG virtual devices only. Changing to Standard Appium requires re-recording; no universal per-flow speed/stability guarantee is implied.

optionExplanations.A: Enhanced runs on VMG virtual devices only.
optionExplanations.B: Enhanced tests are executable on VMG.
optionExplanations.C: A paid Appium license is not the documented execution trade-off.
optionExplanations.D: Enhanced is a mobile app mode.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What limitation does Testim document for its Standard Appium compatibility recording mode?

options.text: Some hybrid/webview flows may not be fully recordable; verify the required flow and mode.
Because hybrid apps are not supported by Testim Mobile at all, in any mode.
Because Appium mode only works on iOS.
Because hybrid apps require a separate Testim license.

practiceQuiz.hint: A Testim recording limitation is not a claim that all Appium hybrid testing is impossible.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Testim warns of mode-specific recording gaps. Enhanced supports documented frameworks on VMG, but neither app type nor framework name proves a particular flow works.

optionExplanations.A: The documented limitation concerns particular recorded flows.
optionExplanations.B: Testim Mobile supports documented hybrid frameworks.
optionExplanations.C: Standard Appium mode is not iOS-only.
optionExplanations.D: The cited limitation is recording capability, not a separate hybrid license.

quickRecap.value: AI automation (Smart Locators, visual validation) extended to native/hybrid/cross-platform mobile apps.
Java or Kotlin / Objective-C or Swift.
VMG virtual-device execution only; switching mode needs re-recording. Performance/stability varies.
Configured local/physical/virtual or other-grid execution; verify driver/build and recording capabilities.
